presentation.title: Grandchild Emergency Call
presentation.summary: An unfamiliar caller claims to be a grandchild who was arrested after a car accident. The caller and a supposed attorney use fear, secrecy, and an urgent gift-card demand to keep the learner from verifying the story.
presentation.practiceGoal: End suspicious contact and verify the family member or legal claim through a known, independently located contact before providing information or money.

warningSigns.sign: A frightened caller uses a family title but does not provide a name.
The caller asks that parents or other relatives not be contacted.
The caller and supposed attorney resist independent verification and ask the learner to stay on the line.
A second person uses legal authority and an urgent courthouse deadline to increase pressure.
The supposed attorney claims that bail or bond must be paid using gift cards.
Gift cards, wire transfers, cryptocurrency, and courier pickup are unusual payment requests that should trigger a stop-and-verify response.

finalReview.safestAction: End the call and independently contact the family member, another trusted relative, or the courthouse using contact information the caller did not provide.

realWorldActions.action: Do not supply a relative's name or other identity details to an unfamiliar caller.
Use a saved family number or a family code word to verify identity.
Locate courthouse or law-enforcement contact information independently before trusting a legal claim.
Remember that legitimate courts and attorneys do not collect bail using gift cards.
If a store employee questions an unusual gift-card purchase, pause and explain the situation before paying.

artifact.callStatus: Incoming call from an unfamiliar number
artifact.heading: A frightened caller claims to be family
artifact.message: Grandma? Grandpa? It's me. I was in a car accident and the police arrested me. My phone was damaged, so I'm calling from someone else's phone.
artifact.transcript: A frightened young person calls from an unfamiliar number and says, "Grandma? Grandpa? It's me. I was in a car accident and the police arrested me. My phone was damaged, so I'm calling from someone else's phone." The caller does not provide a name.

scene.question: How would you respond before the caller has identified themselves?
scene.description: The caller sounds frightened and describes an emergency, but you do not yet know who is calling.

warningSigns.sign: The call comes from an unfamiliar number.
The caller uses a family title but does not give a name.
Fear and urgency make it harder to pause and verify.

choice.title: Supply a possible grandchild's name
choice.subtitle: Ask whether the caller is the relative you are thinking of.

feedback.heading: The caller adopts the identity you supplied
feedback.consequence: The caller immediately answers, "Yes, that's me," and continues using the name as part of the emergency story.
feedback.explanation: Offering a name gives an unknown caller information they can use. It does not verify who is calling.

warningSigns.sign: The caller did not provide a name before you suggested one.
The caller accepts the identity without providing independent proof.

choice.title: Ask the caller to identify themselves
choice.subtitle: Request a name without offering one.

feedback.heading: The caller avoids the identity question
feedback.consequence: The caller says they are too shaken up to answer clearly and redirects attention to the accident and arrest.
feedback.explanation: Not supplying a name is cautious, but an unclear answer is not verification. The safest next step is still to use a known family number.

warningSigns.sign: The caller avoids a direct identity question.
The emergency is used to move attention away from verification.

choice.title: Hang up and call the saved number
choice.subtitle: Contact the grandchild using a number you already know.

feedback.heading: You switched to a trusted contact method
feedback.consequence: The unfamiliar caller can no longer control the identity check.
feedback.explanation: Ending the unknown call and using a saved number is a direct, independent way to verify the emergency.

warningSigns.sign: The original caller never provided a name.
The emergency claim came from an unfamiliar number.

artifact.heading: The caller uses the name and asks for secrecy
artifact.message: Yes, that's me. Please don't tell Mom or Dad. They'll panic, and they'll be furious with me. I just need you to help me get home before they find out.
artifact.transcript: After the learner supplies a possible grandchild's name, the caller adopts it by saying, "Yes, that's me." The caller repeats that the car accident led to an arrest and says, "Please don't tell Mom or Dad. They'll panic, and they'll be furious with me. I just need you to help me get home before they find out." The caller adds, "The attorney helping me is here. They can explain what needs to happen."

scene.question: What would you do after the caller adopts the name and asks for secrecy?
scene.description: The caller has not proved their identity and now wants to prevent contact with the people who could verify the story.

warningSigns.sign: The caller uses a name that the learner supplied.
The caller asks that Mom, Dad, and other family members not be contacted.
The caller introduces an attorney before the family story is verified.

choice.title: Agree to keep the situation secret
choice.subtitle: Continue without contacting the parents or another relative.

feedback.heading: Secrecy gives the caller more control
feedback.consequence: The caller says the attorney will explain everything and hands the phone to a second person.
feedback.explanation: It is understandable to want to protect a loved one, but secrecy isolates you from the people most able to confirm the story.

warningSigns.sign: The caller asks you to hide an alleged emergency from close family.
The caller controls the introduction of the supposed attorney.

choice.title: Require verification before helping
choice.subtitle: State that you will not continue until the identity and emergency are checked.

feedback.heading: You set and hold a safe boundary
feedback.consequence: The caller asks you not to hang up, but you end the call and verify independently.
feedback.explanation: A verification boundary protects you only when you follow through using a known contact method.

warningSigns.sign: The caller resists ending the call.
The caller wants to remain involved in the verification process.

choice.title: Contact another family member
choice.subtitle: End the call and use a known number to check the story.

feedback.heading: You broke the secrecy request
feedback.consequence: A trusted family member can verify whether the alleged grandchild is safe.
feedback.explanation: Independent family contact removes the caller's control over the story.

warningSigns.sign: The caller specifically tried to prevent family contact.
The emergency depended on secrecy.

artifact.callerStatus: Identity, role, and legal claim not verified
artifact.callStatus: The distressed caller has handed the phone to a second person
artifact.heading: A supposed attorney explains the arrest and urgent bond
artifact.message: This is Daniel Mercer. I'm the court-appointed attorney assisting your grandchild. They were arrested after the accident and are currently being held until bond is paid.
artifact.transcript: The distressed caller says, "The attorney helping me is here. They can explain what needs to happen," and hands the phone to a second person. The second person says, "This is Daniel Mercer. I'm the court-appointed attorney assisting your grandchild. They were arrested after the accident and are currently being held until bond is paid." He claims that a judge set an urgent bond, that payment must be arranged before the courthouse closes, and that contacting the parents could delay the release.

scene.question: How would you respond to the supposed attorney's urgent bond demand?
scene.description: The second person sounds confident, but everything known about the attorney, arrest, and bond still comes from the same unverified call.

warningSigns.sign: The distressed caller introduces the only person claiming to confirm the emergency.
The supposed attorney creates a deadline tied to the courthouse closing.
The supposed attorney discourages contact with family.

choice.title: Request case details, end the call, and verify
choice.subtitle: Locate official courthouse contact information independently.

feedback.heading: You separated the claim from its verification
feedback.consequence: The supposed attorney cannot control which official number you call or remain on the line during the check.
feedback.explanation: Names and case details supplied by a caller are claims to check, not proof. Ending the call is essential.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed attorney pressures you to act before independently checking the case.
The courthouse deadline comes only from the caller.

choice.title: Agree to arrange payment immediately
choice.subtitle: Let the supposed attorney control the payment process.

feedback.heading: The supposed attorney moves from urgency to payment instructions
feedback.consequence: The supposed attorney says the bond office requires prepaid payment cards and tells you how to obtain them.
feedback.explanation: Agreeing to pay before verification allows the caller to choose a payment method that benefits the scam.

warningSigns.sign: Payment is requested before the family identity or legal claim is verified.
The supposed attorney controls the entire payment route.

choice.title: Say that family must be contacted first
choice.subtitle: Tell the supposed attorney that you will verify with the parents or another relative.

feedback.heading: A safe intention still needs follow-through
feedback.consequence: The supposed attorney immediately pressures you not to make that call.
feedback.explanation: Contacting family is the safe plan, but remaining on the call allows more pressure. The follow-up decision tests whether you end contact and follow through.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed attorney tries to prevent family contact.
The release deadline is used to challenge a safe decision.

artifact.heading: The supposed attorney tries to stop family contact
artifact.message: Do not call the parents right now. That could delay the release, and the courthouse closes soon. Stay on the line so we can finish this.
artifact.transcript: After the learner says that the parents or another family member must be contacted, the supposed attorney responds, "Do not call the parents right now. That could delay the release, and the courthouse closes soon. Stay on the line so we can finish this."

scene.question: Will you follow through with independent family verification?
scene.description: The pressure does not provide proof. It tries to keep you inside the caller's version of events.

warningSigns.sign: The caller directly discourages contact with the parents.
The courthouse deadline is repeated to prevent a pause.
The caller asks you to remain on the line.

choice.title: End the call and contact family
choice.subtitle: Use a known number and do not let the caller participate.

feedback.heading: You followed through on verification
feedback.consequence: The supposed attorney loses the ability to pressure you while the family checks the story.
feedback.explanation: Safe plans remain protective when you follow them despite urgency or authority pressure.

warningSigns.sign: The caller tried to stop you from contacting family.
The caller wanted to stay connected during the decision.

choice.title: Give in to the pressure and continue
choice.subtitle: Stay on the line without contacting family.

feedback.heading: The supposed attorney keeps control
feedback.consequence: The supposed attorney immediately provides prepaid-card payment instructions.
feedback.explanation: Giving up independent verification lets the caller turn emotional and authority pressure into a payment demand.

warningSigns.sign: The caller prevented contact with the people most able to verify the emergency.
The conversation moves directly from secrecy to payment.

artifact.callStatus: Learner is still at home with the call connected
artifact.heading: The supposed attorney demands prepaid cards
artifact.message: The bond office cannot accept a personal check over the phone. You'll need to purchase prepaid payment cards from a nearby store. Stay on the line, and I'll explain how to submit the card numbers to the bond account.
artifact.transcript: The learner is still at home. The supposed attorney says, "The bond office cannot accept a personal check over the phone. You'll need to purchase prepaid payment cards from a nearby store. Stay on the line, and I'll explain how to submit the card numbers to the bond account."

scene.question: What would you do after the gift-card instructions?
scene.description: Legitimate courts and attorneys do not collect bail using gift cards. The caller wants you to stay connected while leaving home to make the purchase.

warningSigns.sign: Gift cards are presented as a way to pay an urgent bond.
The supposed attorney asks for the card numbers.
The caller instructs you to stay on the line while traveling to a store.

choice.title: Refuse the gift-card demand
choice.subtitle: State that legitimate courts and attorneys do not demand gift cards.

feedback.heading: You recognized the payment warning sign
feedback.consequence: You end the call without leaving home or providing money.
feedback.explanation: Refusing the demand stops the scammer's payment path. Independent verification can begin after the call ends.

warningSigns.sign: The payment method does not fit a legitimate court process.
The caller asks for redeemable card numbers.

choice.title: End the call and verify independently
choice.subtitle: Contact the courthouse or family using information you locate yourself.

feedback.heading: You left the caller's payment process
feedback.consequence: The supposed attorney cannot direct the verification or keep you from contacting family.
feedback.explanation: Independent contact is safer than checking a claim while the person requesting money remains involved.

warningSigns.sign: The caller tried to combine verification and payment in one controlled conversation.
The caller discouraged contact with family and official sources.

choice.title: Agree to travel to a nearby store
choice.subtitle: Keep the supposed attorney on the phone while going to buy the cards.

feedback.heading: The caller keeps the payment moving
feedback.consequence: You drive to a nearby store while the caller remains on the phone and repeats the courthouse deadline.
feedback.explanation: Remaining connected preserves the scammer's pressure and reduces the opportunity to ask someone else for advice.

warningSigns.sign: The caller directs your movement to a new location.
The caller remains on the phone during the purchase.

artifact.heading: A store employee notices the gift-card purchase
artifact.message: Are you buying these because someone on the phone told you to? That's a common scam. Courts and attorneys do not collect bail using gift cards.
artifact.transcript: After agreeing to the instructions, the learner drives to a nearby store while the supposed attorney remains on the phone. At checkout, the learner attempts to purchase the prepaid cards. A store employee notices the large gift-card purchase and asks, "Are you buying these because someone on the phone told you to? That's a common scam. Courts and attorneys do not collect bail using gift cards."

scene.question: How would you respond to the employee's warning before completing the purchase?
scene.description: The employee has been introduced at checkout and is offering a chance to stop before any card numbers are shared.

warningSigns.sign: The purchase is being made only because of instructions from an unfamiliar caller.
The caller has stayed on the phone from home to the store.
A store employee recognizes the payment request as a common scam.

choice.title: Explain the situation and accept help
choice.subtitle: Pause the purchase and tell the employee about the emergency call.

feedback.heading: You accepted help before paying
feedback.consequence: The employee helps stop the purchase and encourages you to contact family independently.
feedback.explanation: Scammers rely on isolation. A trusted second perspective can interrupt the pressure without blaming the person targeted.

warningSigns.sign: The caller wanted the purchase completed while staying on the phone.
The payment request matches a scam pattern recognized by the employee.

choice.title: Step away and call the saved family number
choice.subtitle: End the suspicious call and contact the grandchild directly.

feedback.heading: You stopped before completing the purchase
feedback.consequence: The real grandchild can confirm whether any accident or arrest occurred.
feedback.explanation: It is not too late to switch to independent verification. Stopping before payment prevents financial loss.

warningSigns.sign: The caller tried to remain involved through the entire purchase.
The employee's warning confirms the payment method is suspicious.

choice.title: Ignore the warning and provide the card numbers
choice.subtitle: Complete the purchase and read the numbers to the caller.

feedback.heading: The card value is transferred to the scammer
feedback.consequence: The caller redeems the cards, and the money may not be recoverable.
feedback.explanation: Urgency and concern for family can overwhelm anyone. The employee's warning was a final opportunity to stop and verify before sharing the numbers.

warningSigns.sign: The supposed attorney asks for gift-card numbers instead of a legitimate payment.
The caller's instructions conflict with the employee's clear warning.

artifact.transcript: After ending the unfamiliar call, the learner calls the grandchild using a saved number. The real family member confirms there was no accident or arrest.
